Find, **in radians**, the argument of $z=-11+8\text{i}.$ Round your final answer to **two decimal places**.

**Hint**: The argument of a complex number is in the range $[0,2\pi ).$

feedback.worked_solution:
Let's plot $z$ in the complex plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13930486/assets/d3b5558c0268843618c52c588ffcf1c8012189041b17d52fadd6fe74c3526700.png)

The complex number $z$ lies in the second quadrant of the complex plane. Hence $\frac{\pi }{2}<arg⁡(z)<\pi .$ 

If $\alpha $ is the angle that $z$ makes with the negative real axis, then

$$
\begin{aligned}tan⁡\alpha  & =\frac{8}{11} \\ \alpha  & =arctan⁡(\frac{8}{11}) \\  & =0.628\text{ }796\text{ }…\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =arg⁡(z)=\pi -0.628\text{ }796\text{ }…≈2.51,
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
